input.quote: (ii) the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards;
input.rationale: Section 9(b) contains a genuine express performance warranty from Kubient that meets and exceeds our preferred position on the material terms: the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards (p0034), services will comply with the Agreement and be "free from errors that materially affect their utility" (p0038), the product and service will be free of viruses, Trojan Horses, worms, back doors and similar malicious routines (p0036), and Kubient will comply with all applicable Laws throughout the Term (p0041). Duration is better than preferred: these are continuing warranties/covenants running for the whole Term rather than a 12-month or 90-day window. The Section 13 disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty — it is twice qualified ("Except as expressly set forth herein" and "except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement"), so it disclaims only implied warranties and the revenue/profit guarantee, and does not reach walk-away "AS IS" territory. Noted but not flagged: there is no express repair/re-perform/refund remedy sentence. That is a sub-element short of the preferred wording only, and its absence works in our favour — we keep our full contractual remedies (direct damages, plus termination on 30 days' uncured material breach under 4(b)) rather than being confined to a capped exclusive remedy. No redline warranted.
